Name: Feedbin
Description: RSS reader
Introduction: The Feedbin API is a powerful tool that allows developers to integrate Feedbin's RSS reader functionality into their own applications. This API provides the following functions: 1) Get all of a user's feeds. 2) Get all of a user's unread entries. 3) Retrieve entries from a specified feed by timestamp. 4) Star, mark as read, or un-mark as read an entry. 5) Retrieve metadata about a feed, including its title, URL, and icon. With these functions, developers can create innovative, user-friendly applications that streamline the RSS reading experience.
Functions:
1. Name: getUserFeeds
Description: Retrieves all of a user's feeds.
Input: None
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each representing a feed. Each object contains the following fields:
- id: Integer. The unique ID of the feed.
- title: String. The title of the feed.
- feed_url: String. The URL of the feed.
- site_url: String. The URL of the feed's website.
- is_spark: Boolean. Indicates whether the feed is a Spark feed.
- last_updated_at: String. The timestamp of the feed's last update.

2. Name: getUserUnreadEntries
Description: Retrieves all of a user's unread entries.
Input: None
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each representing an unread entry. Each object contains the following fields:
- id: Integer. The unique ID of the entry.
- title: String. The title of the entry.
- author: String. The author of the entry.
- content: String. The content of the entry.
- url: String. The URL of the entry.
- feed_id: Integer. The ID of the feed that the entry belongs to.
- published: String. The timestamp of the entry's publication.
- created_at: String. The timestamp of the entry's creation.
- updated_at: String. The timestamp of the entry's last update.

3. Name: getFeedEntriesByTimestamp
Description: Retrieves entries from a specified feed by timestamp.
Input: 
- feed_id: Required. Integer. The ID of the feed to retrieve entries from.
- timestamp: Required. String. The timestamp to retrieve entries from, in the format "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ".
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each representing an entry. Each object contains the following fields:
- id: Integer. The unique ID of the entry.
- title: String. The title of the entry.
- author: String. The author of the entry.
- content: String. The content of the entry.
- url: String. The URL of the entry.
- feed_id: Integer. The ID of the feed that the entry belongs to.
- published: String. The timestamp of the entry's publication.
- created_at: String. The timestamp of the entry's creation.
- updated_at: String. The timestamp of the entry's last update.

4. Name: markEntry
Description: Stars, marks as read, or un-marks as read an entry.
Input: 
- entry_id: Required. Integer. The ID of the entry to mark.
- star: Optional. Boolean. Indicates whether to star the entry.
- read: Optional. Boolean. Indicates whether to mark the entry as read.
Output: Returns a JSON object representing the updated entry. The object contains the same fields as the entry object returned by the getFeedEntriesByTimestamp function.

5. Name: getFeedMetadata
Description: Retrieves metadata about a feed, including its title, URL, and icon.
Input: 
- feed_id: Required. Integer. The ID of the feed to retrieve metadata for.
Output: Returns a JSON object representing the feed's metadata. The object contains the following fields:
- title: String. The title of the feed.
- feed_url: String. The URL of the feed.
- site_url: String. The URL of the feed's website.
- icon_url: String. The URL of the feed's icon.

Name: Universalis
Description: Final Fantasy XIV market board data
Introduction: The Universalis API is an essential resource for any Final Fantasy XIV player looking to stay up-to-date on market board data. This API provides accurate price data for all items sold on the market board. It offers the following features: 1) Retrieve current market prices for an item. 2) Retrieve historical market prices for an item. 3) Search for items by their name in multiple languages. 4) Retrieve a list of users who are selling an item. Additionally, this API allows for frequent updates, making it an integral tool for helping players make informed decisions when buying and selling items on the market board.
Functions:
1. Name: getCurrentPrices
    Description: Retrieve the current market prices for an item.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - world: String. The name of the world to retrieve prices for.
        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item to retrieve prices for.
    Output: JSON object with the following keys:
        - world: String. The name of the world the prices are for.
        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item the prices are for.
        - prices: JSON object with the following keys:
            - NQ: JSON object with the following keys:
                - minPrice: Integer. The minimum price for the item in NQ quality.
                - maxPrice: Integer. The maximum price for the item in NQ quality.
                - averagePrice: Integer. The average price for the item in NQ quality.
            - HQ: JSON object with the following keys:
                - minPrice: Integer. The minimum price for the item in HQ quality.
                - maxPrice: Integer. The maximum price for the item in HQ quality.
                - averagePrice: Integer. The average price for the item in HQ quality.

2. Name: getHistoricalPrices
    Description: Retrieve the historical market prices for an item.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - world: String. The name of the world to retrieve prices for.
        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item to retrieve prices for.
        - numDays: Integer. The number of days of historical data to retrieve.
    Output: JSON object with the following keys:
        - world: String. The name of the world the prices are for.
        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item the prices are for.
        - prices: JSON array of JSON objects with the following keys:
            - timestamp: Integer. The Unix timestamp of the historical price data.
            - NQ: JSON object with the following keys:
                - minPrice: Integer. The minimum price for the item in NQ quality.
                - maxPrice: Integer. The maximum price for the item in NQ quality.
                - averagePrice: Integer. The average price for the item in NQ quality.
            - HQ: JSON object with the following keys:
                - minPrice: Integer. The minimum price for the item in HQ quality.
                - maxPrice: Integer. The maximum price for the item in HQ quality.
                - averagePrice: Integer. The average price for the item in HQ quality.

3. Name: searchItem
    Description: Search for items by their name in multiple languages.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - name: String. The name of the item to search for.
        - language: String. The language to search in. Valid values are "en", "fr", "de", and "ja".
    Output: JSON array of JSON objects with the following keys:
        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item.
        - name: String. The name of the item in the specified language.
        - icon: String. The URL of the item's icon.

4. Name: getSellers
    Description: Retrieve a list of users who are selling an item.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - world: String. The name of the world to retrieve sellers for.
        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item to retrieve sellers for.
    Output: JSON array of JSON objects with the following keys:
        - sellerID: Integer. The ID of the seller.
        - sellerName: String. The name of the seller.
        - world: String. The name of the world the seller is on.
        - pricePerUnit: Integer. The price per unit the seller is selling the item for.
        - quantity: Integer. The quantity of the item the seller is selling.

Description: Cryptocurrency Exchange based in South Africa
Introduction: VALR is a powerful Cryptocurrency Exchange API that enables seamless trading and exchange of cryptocurrencies for users all around the world. The API provides a range of functions, including: 1) Real-time cryptocurrency market data, enabling clients to make data-driven decisions. 2) Trading capabilities to place orders, track order books, manage trades in real-time. 3) Withdrawal and deposit functionalities for secure movement of funds. 4) Customizable account management features, including balance summaries and transaction histories. With VALR API, you can easily integrate digital asset trading into your app or software, empower your clients to invest and trade in cryptocurrencies, and drive business growth.

1. Name: getMarketSummary
Description: Retrieves the summary of the specified market.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- market: String. The market symbol (e.g. BTCZAR).
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- market: String. The market symbol.
- high: Float. The highest price of the market in the last 24 hours.
- low: Float. The lowest price of the market in the last 24 hours.
- volume: Float. The total volume of the market in the last 24 hours.
- last: Float. The last traded price of the market.
- bid: Float. The highest bid price of the market.
- ask: Float. The lowest ask price of the market.

2. Name: getOrderBook
Description: Retrieves the order book of the specified market.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- market: String. The market symbol (e.g. BTCZAR).
- limit: Optional. Integer. The maximum number of orders to retrieve. Default is 100.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- market: String. The market symbol.
- bids: Array of JSON objects. Each object has the following keys:
  - price: Float. The bid price.
  - quantity: Float. The bid quantity.
- asks: Array of JSON objects. Each object has the following keys:
  - price: Float. The ask price.
  - quantity: Float. The ask quantity.

3. Name: placeOrder
Description: Places an order on the specified market.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- market: String. The market symbol (e.g. BTCZAR).
- side: String. The order side, either "buy" or "sell".
- quantity: Float. The order quantity.
- price: Float. The order price.
- postOnly: Optional. Boolean. If true, the order will only be placed if it does not immediately match with an existing order. Default is false.
- clientId: Optional. String. A unique identifier for the order. Default is a randomly generated UUID.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- orderId: String. The ID of the placed order.

4. Name: getOrderDetails
Description: Retrieves the details of the specified order.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- orderId: String. The ID of the order.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- orderId: String. The ID of the order.
- market: String. The market symbol.
- side: String. The order side, either "buy" or "sell".
- quantity: Float. The order quantity.
- price: Float. The order price.
- status: String. The order status, either "open", "filled", "cancelled", or "rejected".
- createdAt: String. The timestamp when the order was created.
- updatedAt: String. The timestamp when the order was last updated.

5. Name: getAccountBalances
Description: Retrieves the balances of the authenticated user's account.
Input: None.
Output: Array of JSON objects. Each object has the following keys:
- currency: String. The currency symbol.
- balance: Float. The available balance of the currency.
- reserved: Float. The reserved balance of the currency.
- total: Float. The total balance of the currency (balance + reserved).

6. Name: withdrawFunds
Description: Withdraws funds from the authenticated user's account.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- currency: String. The currency symbol.
- amount: Float. The amount to withdraw.
- address: String. The destination address.
- tag: Optional. String. The destination tag (if applicable).
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- withdrawalId: String. The ID of the withdrawal request.

7. Name: getTransactionHistory
Description: Retrieves the transaction history of the authenticated user's account.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following keys:
- currency: String. The currency symbol.
- limit: Optional. Integer. The maximum number of transactions to retrieve. Default is 100.
- offset: Optional. Integer. The offset of the first transaction to retrieve. Default is 0.
Output: Array of JSON objects. Each object has the following keys:
- transactionId: String. The ID of the transaction.
- currency: String. The currency symbol.
- amount: Float. The amount of the transaction.
- type: String. The type of the transaction, either "deposit" or "withdrawal".
- status: String. The status of the transaction, either "pending", "completed", or "failed".
- createdAt: String. The timestamp when the transaction was created.
- updatedAt: String. The timestamp when the transaction was last updated.

Description: Historical data regarding holidays
Introduction: The Holidays API is a comprehensive resource for historical data regarding holidays worldwide. With a wide range of functions, the Holidays API provides access to information on public holidays, religious holidays, and observances. Functions include: 1) Retrieve a list of holidays for a specific date range. 2) Retrieve a list of holidays for a specific country or region. 3) Retrieve detailed information about a specific holiday, including its name, date, and addition information such as whether it is a national holiday or observance. With its wealth of information, the Holidays API is ideal for developers seeking to build applications that incorporate holiday data.

- "start_date": String. The start date of the date range in YYYY-MM-DD format.
- "end_date": String. The end date of the date range in YYYY-MM-DD format.
- "country": Optional. String. The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code for the country to retrieve holidays for. If not provided, holidays for all countries will be returned.
- "region": Optional. String. The region within the country to retrieve holidays for. If not provided, holidays for the entire country will be returned.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a holiday within the specified date range. Each object contains the following keys:
- "name": String. The name of the holiday.
- "date": String. The date of the holiday in YYYY-MM-DD format.
- "observed": String. The date the holiday is observed, if different from the date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
- "public": Boolean. Whether the holiday is a public holiday or not.
- "country": String. The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code for the country the holiday is observed in.
- "region": String. The region within the country the holiday is observed in.

- "observed": String. The date the holiday is observed, if different from the date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

- "country": String. The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code for the country the holiday is observed in.
- "region": String. The region within the country the holiday is observed in.

- "description": String. A description of the holiday.

Description: Social beer sharing
Introduction: The Untappd API (Application Programming Interface) offers comprehensive features for beer enthusiasts to interact, share, and explore new varieties of beer. This API is used to gain access to user reviews, beer ratings, and venues, as well as data for creating dynamic beer menus. This API provides the following features: 1) Retrieve specific beer information, such as name, rating, and style. 2) Discover local beer establishments and review recommendations based on user preferences. 3) Create custom beer menus based on user input.

- beer_description: String. A description of the beer.
- beer_abv: Float. The alcohol by volume (ABV) of the beer.
- beer_ibu: Integer. The International Bitterness Units (IBU) of the beer.

Name: SpaceX
Description: GraphQL, Company, Ships, launchpad and launch data
Introduction: The SpaceX API is a comprehensive resource for accessing and manipulating data related to SpaceX rocket ships, launches, and launchpads. It utilizes GraphQL, a flexible and efficient querying language that allows users to request only the specific data they need. Some of the main functions provided by the SpaceX API include: 1) Accessing information about the company and its history. 2) Retrieving details about individual rocket ships, including their current location and launch history. 3) Accessing data about upcoming and past launches, including launch dates and mission goals. Overall, the SpaceX API is an indispensable tool for anyone looking to stay abreast of the latest developments in commercial spaceflight.
Functions:
1. Name: getCompanyInfo
Description: Retrieves information about SpaceX as a company, including its history and mission statement.
Input: None
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following fields:
- name: The name of the company (string)
- founder: The name of the company's founder (string)
- founded: The year the company was founded (integer)
- employees: The number of employees currently working for the company (integer)
- vehicles: The number of vehicles in the company's fleet (integer)
- launch_sites: The number of launch sites owned by the company (integer)
- test_sites: The number of test sites owned by the company (integer)
- ceo: The name of the company's CEO (string)
- cto: The name of the company's CTO (string)
- coo: The name of the company's COO (string)
- cto_propulsion: The name of the company's CTO of Propulsion (string)
- valuation: The company's current valuation in USD (integer)
- headquarters: A JSON object containing information about the company's headquarters, including its address and city (string)

2. Name: getRocket
Description: Retrieves information about a specific rocket ship, including its name, type, and launch history.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- id: The unique identifier of the rocket (string)
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following fields:
- id: The unique identifier of the rocket (string)
- name: The name of the rocket (string)
- type: The type of the rocket (string)
- active: Whether the rocket is currently active (boolean)
- stages: The number of stages the rocket has (integer)
- boosters: The number of boosters the rocket has (integer)
- cost_per_launch: The cost of launching the rocket (integer)
- success_rate_pct: The percentage of successful launches for the rocket (float)
- first_flight: The date of the rocket's first flight (string)
- country: The country of origin for the rocket (string)
- company: The name of the company that built the rocket (string)
- height: A JSON object containing information about the rocket's height, including its meters and feet (float)
- diameter: A JSON object containing information about the rocket's diameter, including its meters and feet (float)
- mass: A JSON object containing information about the rocket's mass, including its kg and lb (float)
- payload_weights: An array of JSON objects containing information about the rocket's payload weights, including their id, name, and kg (float)
- first_stage: A JSON object containing information about the rocket's first stage, including its engines, fuel amount, and reusable status (boolean)
- second_stage: A JSON object containing information about the rocket's second stage, including its engines and fuel amount
- engines: A JSON object containing information about the rocket's engines, including their type, number, and thrust (float)
- landing_legs: A JSON object containing information about the rocket's landing legs, including their number and material
- wikipedia: The URL of the rocket's Wikipedia page (string)
- description: A brief description of the rocket (string)
- launches: An array of JSON objects containing information about the rocket's past and future launches, including their id, name, and launch date

3. Name: getLaunch
Description: Retrieves information about a specific launch, including its name, date, and mission details.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- id: The unique identifier of the launch (string)
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following fields:
- id: The unique identifier of the launch (string)
- name: The name of the launch (string)
- flight_number: The flight number of the launch (integer)
- date_utc: The date and time of the launch in UTC format (string)
- date_local: The date and time of the launch in local time (string)
- success: Whether the launch was successful (boolean)
- rocket: A JSON object containing information about the rocket used in the launch, including its id and name
- mission: A JSON object containing information about the mission of the launch, including its name, details, and payloads
- launchpad: A JSON object containing information about the launchpad used in the launch, including its id, name, and location
- details: Additional details about the launch (string)
- upcoming: Whether the launch is upcoming (boolean)

4. Name: getNextLaunch
Description: Retrieves information about the next scheduled launch.
Input: None
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the same fields as the getLaunch function, but only for the next scheduled launch.

5. Name: getPastLaunches
Description: Retrieves information about past launches, with optional filtering by date range and success status.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following fields:
- start_date_utc: The start date of the date range to filter by, in UTC format (string)
- end_date_utc: The end date of the date range to filter by, in UTC format (string)
- success: Whether to filter by successful launches only (boolean)
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each containing the same fields as the getLaunch function, but only for past launches that match the specified filters.

6. Name: getUpcomingLaunches
Description: Retrieves information about upcoming launches, with optional filtering by date range.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following fields:
- start_date_utc: The start date of the date range to filter by, in UTC format (string)
- end_date_utc: The end date of the date range to filter by, in UTC format (string)
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each containing the same fields as the getLaunch function, but only for upcoming launches that match the specified filters.

This API offers a comprehensive set of functions, such as: 1) Retrieve the list of blogs owned by a user. 2) Retrieve the posts for a particular blog. 3) Publish new blog posts or update existing ones. 4) Manage comments and notifications. With the Blogger API, developers can create innovative applications that allow users to engage with their favorite blogs and share their ideas with the world.

Description: Retrieve the list of blogs owned by a user.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- userId: String. The ID of the user whose blogs are being retrieved.

- id: String. The ID of the blog.
- name: String. The name of the blog.
- description: String. The description of the blog.
- url: String. The URL of the blog.

2. Name: listPosts
Description: Retrieve the posts for a particular blog.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- blogId: String. The ID of the blog whose posts are being retrieved.

- id: String. The ID of the post.
- title: String. The title of the post.
- content: String. The content of the post.
- published: String. The date and time the post was published.
- updated: String. The date and time the post was last updated.

- blogId: String. The ID of the blog where the post will be published.

- id: String. The ID of the newly created post.

Name: Musixmatch
Description: Music
Introduction: The Musixmatch API is a platform that allows developers to retrieve music-related data and lyrics from a massive database of over 14 million song lyrics and artist information. Some of the functionalities this API offers include: 1) Searching for lyrics based on a song title, artist, or even a line from the song. 2) Matching lyrics to their corresponding audio tracks. 3) Getting detailed information about a specific artist, including their biography, albums, and songs. 4) Translating lyrics and displaying them in different languages. With the Musixmatch API, developers can create music-related applications or websites that provide users with a comprehensive resource for all things related to music.
Functions:
1. Name: searchLyrics
Description: This function allows users to search for lyrics based on a song title, artist, or even a line from the song.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- q: String. The search query.
- f_has_lyrics: String. Whether to filter results to only include songs with lyrics. Possible values are "1" (yes) or "0" (no).
- f_artist_id: Integer. The ID of the artist to filter results by.
- f_music_genre_id: Integer. The ID of the music genre to filter results by.
- page_size: Integer. The number of results to return per page. Maximum value is 100.
- page: Integer. The page number to return. Default value is 1.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a song that matches the search query. Each object contains the following keys:
- track_id: Integer. The ID of the song.
- track_name: String. The name of the song.
- artist_name: String. The name of the artist.
- album_name: String. The name of the album the song belongs to.
- has_lyrics: Integer. Whether the song has lyrics. Possible values are 0 (no) or 1 (yes).
- lyrics_id: Integer. The ID of the lyrics for the song. Only present if the song has lyrics.
- explicit: Integer. Whether the song contains explicit content. Possible values are 0 (no) or 1 (yes).
- instrumental: Integer. Whether the song is instrumental. Possible values are 0 (no) or 1 (yes).
- first_release_date: String. The date the song was first released.
- track_rating: Integer. The rating of the song on Musixmatch, out of 100.

2. Name: getLyrics
Description: This function allows users to retrieve the lyrics for a specific song.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- track_id: Integer. The ID of the song to retrieve the lyrics for.
Output: A JSON object containing the following keys:
- lyrics_id: Integer. The ID of the lyrics.
- lyrics_body: String. The full lyrics of the song.
- script_tracking_url: String. The URL of the script used to track the lyrics views.
- pixel_tracking_url: String. The URL of the pixel used to track the lyrics views.

3. Name: getArtist
Description: This function allows users to retrieve detailed information about a specific artist, including their biography, albums, and songs.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- artist_id: Integer. The ID of the artist to retrieve information for.
Output: A JSON object containing the following keys:
- artist_id: Integer. The ID of the artist.
- artist_name: String. The name of the artist.
- artist_country: String. The country the artist is from.
- artist_rating: Integer. The rating of the artist on Musixmatch, out of 100.
- artist_twitter_url: String. The URL of the artist's Twitter page.
- artist_credits: Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a song the artist has contributed to, and contains the following keys:
  - artist_id: Integer. The ID of the artist.
  - artist_name: String. The name of the artist.
  - artist_mbid: String. The MusicBrainz ID of the artist.
  - artist_type: String. The type of artist. Possible values are "main" or "featured".
  - artist_role: String. The role the artist played in the song. Possible values are "composer", "lyricist", "producer", "remixer", "writer", or "featured".

4. Name: translateLyrics
Description: This function allows users to translate the lyrics of a song into a different language.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- lyrics_id: Integer. The ID of the lyrics to translate.
- target_language: String. The language code of the language to translate the lyrics to. For example, "es" for Spanish or "fr" for French.
Output: A JSON object containing the following keys:
- lyrics_id: Integer. The ID of the original lyrics.
- translated_lyrics_id: Integer. The ID of the translated lyrics.
- translated_lyrics_language: String. The language code of the translated lyrics.
- translated_lyrics_body: String. The full translated lyrics of the song.

        - name: The name of the mount.
        - description: The description of the mount.

Introduction: WeatherAPI provides developers with up-to-date and accurate weather information, as well as other features such as astronomy and geolocation data. With WeatherAPI, you can access multiple functions, including: 1) Real-time weather updates for any location. 2) Historical weather data for past dates. 3) Astronomy data for sunrise and sunset times, moonrise and moonset times, and more. 4) Geolocation data for specific locations based on latitude and longitude coordinates. WeatherAPI's easy-to-use features make it perfect for any developer looking to integrate weather data into their application.

Description: Returns the current weather conditions for a specified location.
Input: { 
        "q": "Required. String. The location to retrieve weather data for, in the format of city name, state/province, and country code (e.g. London, UK).",
        "lang": "Optional. String. The language to return the weather data in, using ISO 639-1 language codes (e.g. en for English, fr for French). Default is English.",
        "unit": "Optional. String. The unit of measurement to return the weather data in, either metric or imperial. Default is metric."
       }
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
        - Location: the name of the location
        - Current: an object containing the current weather conditions, including temperature, feels like temperature, wind speed and direction, humidity, pressure, and more.

2. Name: getHistoricalWeather
Description: Returns the historical weather conditions for a specified location and date.

       }
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
        - Location: the name of the location
        - Historical: an object containing the historical weather conditions for the specified date, including temperature, feels like temperature, wind speed and direction, humidity, pressure, and more.

3. Name: getAstronomyData
Description: Returns the astronomy data for a specified location and date.

        "q": "Required. String. The location to retrieve astronomy data for, in the format of city name, state/province, and country code (e.g. London, UK).",

        "lang": "Optional. String. The language to return the astronomy data in, using ISO 639-1 language codes (e.g. en for English, fr for French). Default is English."
       }
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:

Name: Pinterest
Description: The world's catalog of ideas
Introduction: The Pinterest API (Application Programming Interface) allows developers to integrate Pinterest's unique features into their own websites and applications. With the Pinterest API, users can access the following functions: 1) Searching and finding user boards, pins, and accounts. 2) Retrieving data on user activity, such as boards created or pins saved. 3) Creating new pins with user-generated content. 4) Managing Pinterest boards and their respective pins. This API provides a powerful way to enhance the user experience on a website by incorporating Pinterest's vast database of creative ideas and exciting community.
Functions:
1. Name: searchBoards
Description: This function allows users to search for Pinterest boards based on a query string.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- query: String. The search query.
- limit: Integer. The maximum number of results to return. Default is 25.
Output: An array of board objects, each containing the following information:
- id: String. The unique ID of the board.
- name: String. The name of the board.
- description: String. The description of the board.
- url: String. The URL of the board.
- image_url: String. The URL of the board's cover image.

2. Name: getBoardPins
Description: This function allows users to retrieve all pins from a specific Pinterest board.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- board_id: String. The ID of the board to retrieve pins from.
- limit: Integer. The maximum number of results to return. Default is 25.
Output: An array of pin objects, each containing the following information:
- id: String. The unique ID of the pin.
- image_url: String. The URL of the pin's image.
- description: String. The description of the pin.
- url: String. The URL of the pin.
- board_id: String. The ID of the board that the pin belongs to.

3. Name: getUserBoards
Description: This function allows users to retrieve all boards created by a specific Pinterest user.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- user_id: String. The ID of the user to retrieve boards from.
- limit: Integer. The maximum number of results to return. Default is 25.
Output: An array of board objects, each containing the following information:
- id: String. The unique ID of the board.
- name: String. The name of the board.
- description: String. The description of the board.
- url: String. The URL of the board.
- image_url: String. The URL of the board's cover image.

4. Name: createPin
Description: This function allows users to create a new pin on a specific Pinterest board.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- board_id: String. The ID of the board to create the pin on.
- image_url: String. The URL of the image to use for the pin.
- description: String. The description of the pin.
- link: String. The URL to link the pin to.
Output: A pin object containing the following information:
- id: String. The unique ID of the pin.
- image_url: String. The URL of the pin's image.
- description: String. The description of the pin.
- url: String. The URL of the pin.
- board_id: String. The ID of the board that the pin belongs to.

5. Name: deletePin
Description: This function allows users to delete a specific Pinterest pin.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- pin_id: String. The ID of the pin to delete.
Output: A success message indicating that the pin has been deleted.

Introduction: The OwlBot API is a handy resource for developers who need to incorporate word definitions into their applications. This API allows you to retrieve up-to-date and authoritative definitions along with example sentences and photos, if available. Some of the functions provided by the API include: 1) Retrieving the definition of a word. 2) Getting the part of speech for a word. 3) Grabbing example sentences that use a specified word. 4) Finding an image related to a specific word. Implementing the OwlBot API can enhance the user experience of your application by making it more informative and robust.

    Description: Retrieves the definition of a specified word.

    Description: Retrieves the part of speech for a specified word.
    Input: {"word": "Required. String. The word to retrieve the part of speech for."}
    Output: Returns a JSON object containing the part of speech of the specified word.

3. Name: getExampleSentences
    Description: Retrieves example sentences that use a specified word.
    Input: {"word": "Required. String. The word to retrieve example sentences for."}
    Output: Returns a JSON object containing an array of example sentences that use the specified word.

4. Name: getImage
    Description: Retrieves an image related to a specified word.
    Input: {"word": "Required. String. The word to retrieve an image for."}
    Output: Returns a JSON object containing the URL of an image related to the specified word. If no image is available, the object will contain a message indicating that no image was found.

Name: CircleCI
Description: Automate the software development process using continuous integration and continuous delivery
Introduction: The CircleCI API (Application Programming Interface) is a platform that allows users to automate the software development process using continuous integration and continuous delivery. It provides the following functions: 1) Create and manage projects, workflows, and builds. 2) Access build artifacts, test data, and build logs. 3) Trigger builds through webhooks and API calls. 4) Retrieve performance metrics and historical data on builds. By integrating with CircleCI, developers can increase the speed and reliability of their software delivery while reducing the risk of errors.
Functions:
1. Name: Trigger a New Build
Description: This function allows users to trigger a new build for a specific project and branch.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project to trigger the build for.
- branch: String. The name of the branch to build.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the triggered build, including its build number, status, and URL.

2. Name: Get Build Details
Description: This function allows users to retrieve details about a specific build, including its status, duration, and artifacts.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project that the build belongs to.
- build_num: Integer. The number of the build to retrieve details for.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the build, including its status, duration, and artifacts.

3. Name: List Recent Builds
Description: This function allows users to retrieve a list of recent builds for a specific project.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project to retrieve builds for.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the recent builds, including their build numbers, statuses, and durations.

4. Name: Get Build Artifacts
Description: This function allows users to retrieve the artifacts generated by a specific build.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project that the build belongs to.
- build_num: Integer. The number of the build to retrieve artifacts for.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the build artifacts, including their filenames, sizes, and URLs.

5. Name: List Project Workflows
Description: This function allows users to retrieve a list of workflows for a specific project.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project to retrieve workflows for.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the project workflows, including their names and IDs.

6. Name: Get Workflow Details
Description: This function allows users to retrieve details about a specific workflow, including its status and jobs.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project that the workflow belongs to.
- workflow_id: String. The ID of the workflow to retrieve details for.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the workflow, including its status and jobs.

7. Name: Cancel a Workflow
Description: This function allows users to cancel a specific workflow.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project that the workflow belongs to.
- workflow_id: String. The ID of the workflow to cancel.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the canceled workflow, including its status and jobs.

8. Name: List Project Environments
Description: This function allows users to retrieve a list of environments for a specific project.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project to retrieve environments for.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the project environments, including their names and URLs.

9. Name: Get Environment Details
Description: This function allows users to retrieve details about a specific environment, including its variables and URL.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project that the environment belongs to.
- environment_name: String. The name of the environment to retrieve details for.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the environment, including its variables and URL.

The API provides the following functions: 1) URL shortening: Generate a shortened URL for any long URL with options to customize it. 2) Metrics: Retrieve stats such as clicks, referrers, and geolocation for any shortened URL. 3) Campaigns: Organize multiple links into a single campaign to track performance metrics. Name: Waifu.im
Description: Get waifu pictures from an archive of over 4000 images and multiple tags
Introduction: The Waifu.im API is a versatile tool for obtaining waifu pictures from an extensive database of over 4000 images classified with multiple tags. It offers a range of features that make it easy to access and search this archive, including: 1) Querying the database for images based on multiple tags and sorting options. 2) Retrieving detailed information about individual images. 3) Accessing generated collages of images based on search criteria. With Waifu.im, your app can easily incorporate a high-quality collection of waifu imagery.
Functions:
1. Name: searchImages
Description: Search the database for images based on multiple tags and sorting options.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- tags: String array. The tags to search for.
- limit: Integer. The maximum number of images to return. Default is 10.
- page: Integer. The page number of the results to return. Default is 1.
- order_by: String. The field to order the results by. Options are "id", "score", "width", "height", "file_size", "created_at", "updated_at". Default is "score".
- order_direction: String. The direction to order the results by. Options are "asc" and "desc". Default is "desc".
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing an image. Each object has the following keys:
- id: Integer. The unique ID of the image.
- file_name: String. The name of the image file.
- file_size: Integer. The size of the image file in bytes.
- width: Integer. The width of the image in pixels.
- height: Integer. The height of the image in pixels.
- score: Integer. The score of the image.
- created_at: String. The date and time the image was created.
- updated_at: String. The date and time the image was last updated.
- tags: String array. The tags associated with the image.

2. Name: getImageById
Description: Retrieve detailed information about an individual image by its ID.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. The ID of the image to retrieve.
Output: A JSON object representing the image. The object has the same keys as the objects returned by the searchImages function.

3. Name: getRandomImages
Description: Retrieve a random selection of images from the database.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following keys:
- tags: String array. The tags to filter the images by.
- count: Integer. The number of images to retrieve. Default is 10.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing an image. Each object has the same keys as the objects returned by the searchImages function.

Description: Retrieve a collage of images based on search criteria.

- tags: String array. The tags to filter the images by.

- height: Integer. The height of the collage in pixels.
- count: Integer. The number of images to include in the collage. Default is 10.

- id: Integer. The unique ID of the collage.
- file_name: String. The name of the image file containing the collage.
- file_size: Integer. The size of the image file in bytes.
- width: Integer. The width of the collage in pixels.
- height: Integer. The height of the collage in pixels.
- created_at: String. The date and time the collage was created.
- updated_at: String. The date and time the collage was last updated.

Name: IUCN
Description: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
Introduction: The IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) Red List of Threatened Species API is a powerful resource for biodiversity conservationists and researchers alike. It provides access to the most comprehensive dataset on the conservation status of plant and animal species worldwide. The API provides several major functions, including: 1) Searching for threatened species based on specific criteria such as taxonomy, region, and threat status. 2) Retrieving detailed information about a specific species, including its scientific name, habitat range, conservation status, and conservation actions. 3) Retrieving the list of all threatened species within a specific region or taxonomic group. The IUCN API empowers conservationists and researchers with a tool to track and monitor the status of threatened species, an essential component for developing effective conservation strategies.
Functions:
1. Name: searchSpecies
Description: This function allows users to search for threatened species based on specific criteria such as taxonomy, region, and threat status.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "taxonid": Integer. The taxonomic identifier of the species.
- "region": String. The region where the species is located.
- "category": String. The conservation status category of the species.
Output: A list of species that match the search criteria, including their scientific name, common name, and conservation status.

2. Name: getSpeciesDetails
Description: This function allows users to retrieve detailed information about a specific species, including its scientific name, habitat range, conservation status, and conservation actions.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- "speciesid": Integer. The taxonomic identifier of the species.
Output: A JSON object containing detailed information about the species, including its scientific name, common name, habitat range, conservation status, and conservation actions.

3. Name: listThreatenedSpecies
Description: This function allows users to retrieve the list of all threatened species within a specific region or taxonomic group.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "region": String. The region where the species is located.
- "taxonid": Integer. The taxonomic identifier of the species.
Output: A list of threatened species within the specified region or taxonomic group, including their scientific name, common name, and conservation status.

4. Name: getConservationMeasures
Description: This function allows users to retrieve the conservation measures that have been implemented for a specific species.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- "speciesid": Integer. The taxonomic identifier of the species.
Output: A list of conservation measures that have been implemented for the species, including the measure type, description, and date of implementation.

5. Name: getSpeciesHistory
Description: This function allows users to retrieve the historical conservation status of a specific species.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- "speciesid": Integer. The taxonomic identifier of the species.
Output: A list of the historical conservation status of the species, including the year, category, and criteria used to determine the status.

6. Name: getRedListCategories
Description: This function allows users to retrieve the categories used to determine the conservation status of a species.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following key:
- "language": String. The language in which the categories should be returned. Default is English.
Output: A list of the categories used to determine the conservation status of a species, including their name and description.

Name: Catalogopolis
Description: Doctor Who API
Introduction: Catalogopolis is an API (Application Programming Interface) that provides a wide range of data related to the popular BBC TV series, Doctor Who. Designed for fans of the show, this API allows you to access multiple datasets related to Doctor Who, including the characters, monsters, episodes, quotes, and more. The API offers various functionalities: 1) Retrieve all episodes of Doctor Who by season, writer, director, or original air date. 2) Query all information related to specific characters or monsters by name, species, or appearance. 3) Retrieve quotes by character or episode. The API is easy to use and provides reliable, contextual information for use in websites, mobile apps, and other projects.
Functions:
1. Name: getEpisodes
Description: Retrieve all episodes of Doctor Who based on specified criteria.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- season: Integer. The season number of the episodes to retrieve.
- writer: String. The name of the writer of the episodes to retrieve.
- director: String. The name of the director of the episodes to retrieve.
- airDate: String. The original air date of the episodes to retrieve, in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing an episode. Each object contains the following keys:
- title: String. The title of the episode.
- season: Integer. The season number of the episode.
- episode: Integer. The episode number within the season.
- writer: String. The name of the writer of the episode.
- director: String. The name of the director of the episode.
- airDate: String. The original air date of the episode, in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".
- synopsis: String. A brief summary of the episode.

2. Name: getCharacters
Description: Retrieve all characters of Doctor Who based on specified criteria.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- name: String. The name of the character to retrieve.
- species: String. The species of the character to retrieve.
- appearance: String. The first appearance of the character, in the format "Season X, Episode Y".
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a character. Each object contains the following keys:
- name: String. The name of the character.
- actor: String. The name of the actor who portrayed the character.
- species: String. The species of the character.
- appearance: String. The first appearance of the character, in the format "Season X, Episode Y".
- description: String. A brief description of the character.

3. Name: getMonsters
Description: Retrieve all monsters of Doctor Who based on specified criteria.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- name: String. The name of the monster to retrieve.
- species: String. The species of the monster to retrieve.
- appearance: String. The first appearance of the monster, in the format "Season X, Episode Y".
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a monster. Each object contains the following keys:
- name: String. The name of the monster.
- actor: String. The name of the actor who portrayed the monster.
- species: String. The species of the monster.
- appearance: String. The first appearance of the monster, in the format "Season X, Episode Y".
- description: String. A brief description of the monster.

4. Name: getQuotesByCharacter
Description: Retrieve all quotes spoken by a specific character.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- character: String. The name of the character to retrieve quotes for.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a quote. Each object contains the following keys:
- character: String. The name of the character who spoke the quote.
- episode: String. The title of the episode the quote was spoken in.
- quote: String. The actual quote spoken by the character.

5. Name: getQuotesByEpisode
Description: Retrieve all quotes spoken in a specific episode.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- episode: String. The title of the episode to retrieve quotes for.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a quote. Each object contains the following keys:
- character: String. The name of the character who spoke the quote.
- episode: String. The title of the episode the quote was spoken in.
- quote: String. The actual quote spoken by the character.

- expireDt: String. The date the domain will expire.
- registrarName: String. The name of the domain's registrar.
- registrantName: String. The name of the domain's registrant.
- registrantEmail: String. The email address of the domain's registrant.
- registrantOrganization: String. The organization of the domain's registrant.
- status: String. The status of the domain (e.g. active, inactive, pending, etc.).

2. Name: getDomainDetails

Description: Metacert Link Flagging
Introduction: The Metacert API is a powerful tool designed to help protect users from malicious links and websites. By integrating with the Metacert service, developers can flag and verify links in their own applications before they are accessed by users. The API provides several key functions: 1) Verification of links to ensure they are safe to access. 2) Management of link categories and rules. 3) Access to analytics and detailed reports on user activity. By leveraging the robust features of the Metacert API, applications can provide enhanced security and protection to their users.
Functions:
1. Name: verifyLink
Description: This function verifies whether a given link is safe to access or not.
Input: {"link": "Required. String. The link to be verified."}
Output: Returns a JSON object with the following fields:
- "status": String. Indicates whether the link is safe or not. Possible values are "safe" and "unsafe".
- "category": String. Indicates the category of the link, if available.
- "sub_category": String. Indicates the sub-category of the link, if available.
- "rules": Array of strings. Indicates the rules that the link violates, if any.

2. Name: getLinkCategories
Description: This function retrieves a list of all available link categories.
Input: None
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each representing a link category. Each object has the following fields:
- "name": String. The name of the category.
- "description": String. A brief description of the category.

3. Name: getLinkCategoryRules
Description: This function retrieves a list of all rules associated with a given link category.
Input: {"category": "Required. String. The name of the category."}
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each representing a rule. Each object has the following fields:
- "name": String. The name of the rule.
- "description": String. A brief description of the rule.

4. Name: addLinkCategory
Description: This function adds a new link category to the Metacert service.
Input: {"name": "Required. String. The name of the new category.", "description": "Optional. String. A brief description of the new category."}
Output: Returns a JSON object representing the newly created category. The object has the following fields:
- "name": String. The name of the category.
- "description": String. A brief description of the category.

5. Name: addLinkCategoryRule
Description: This function adds a new rule to a given link category.
Input: {"category": "Required. String. The name of the category to which the rule should be added.", "name": "Required. String. The name of the new rule.", "description": "Optional. String. A brief description of the new rule."}
Output: Returns a JSON object representing the newly created rule. The object has the following fields:
- "name": String. The name of the rule.
- "description": String. A brief description of the rule.

6. Name: getLinkAnalytics
Description: This function retrieves analytics data for a given link.
Input: {"link": "Required. String. The link for which analytics data should be retrieved."}
Output: Returns a JSON object representing the analytics data for the given link. The object has the following fields:
- "clicks": Integer. The total number of clicks on the link.
- "unique_clicks": Integer. The number of unique users who clicked on the link.
- "top_countries": Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a country and has the following fields:
  - "name": String. The name of the country.
  - "clicks": Integer. The number of clicks from that country.
- "top_referrers": Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a referrer and has the following fields:
  - "name": String. The name of the referrer.
  - "clicks": Integer. The number of clicks from that referrer.

Name: Schiphol Airport
Description: Schiphol
Introduction: The Schiphol Airport API is an comprehensive tool that provides real-time information about flights, shops, restaurants, parking options, and other amenities available at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol. The API provides a wide range of functions that includes: 1) Retrieving up to date flight information such as flight departure and arrival times, gate numbers, and flight status. 2) Finding shops, restaurants and other services available in each terminal. 3) Getting parking availability and prices. 4) Accessing route and transportation information to and from the airport. With these features, the Schiphol Airport API is a valuable resource for travelers and businesses alike.
Functions:
1. Name: getFlightInformation
    Description: Retrieves up to date flight information such as flight departure and arrival times, gate numbers, and flight status.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - flightNumber: String. The flight number.
        - date: String. The date of the flight in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".
    Output: JSON object with the following keys:
        - flightNumber: String. The flight number.
        - airline: String. The airline of the flight.
        - scheduledTime: String. The scheduled time of the flight in the format "HH:mm".
        - estimatedTime: String. The estimated time of the flight in the format "HH:mm".
        - gate: String. The gate number of the flight.
        - status: String. The status of the flight.

2. Name: getTerminalServices
    Description: Finds shops, restaurants and other services available in each terminal.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - terminal: String. The terminal code.
    Output: JSON array of JSON objects with the following keys:
        - name: String. The name of the service.
        - category: String. The category of the service.
        - location: String. The location of the service.
        - openingHours: String. The opening hours of the service.

3. Name: getParkingInformation
    Description: Gets parking availability and prices.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - parkingType: String. The type of parking (e.g. "short", "long", "valet").
        - date: String. The date of the parking in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".
        - time: String. The time of the parking in the format "HH:mm".
    Output: JSON object with the following keys:
        - parkingType: String. The type of parking.
        - availability: Integer. The number of available parking spots.
        - price: String. The price of the parking.

4. Name: getTransportationInformation
    Description: Accesses route and transportation information to and from the airport.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - origin: String. The origin of the transportation.
        - destination: String. The destination of the transportation.
    Output: JSON object with the following keys:
        - mode: String. The mode of transportation (e.g. "train", "bus", "taxi").
        - duration: String. The duration of the transportation.
        - price: String. The price of the transportation.

Name: Trace Moe
Description: A useful tool to get the exact scene of an anime from a screenshot
Introduction: The Trace Moe API is a powerful tool for anime enthusiasts who want to quickly and easily identify a particular scene from an anime series. This API uses advanced image recognition technology to analyze a screenshot and provide detailed information about the specific episode, timestamp, and title of the anime. The Trace Moe API provides the following functions: 1) Search for an anime by screenshot; 2) Retrieve detailed metadata for a particular episode; 3) View related media recommendations based on the anime in question. With its intuitive interface and powerful functionality, the Trace Moe API is a must-have tool for any serious anime fan.
Functions:
1. Name: Search
Description: This function allows users to search for an anime by providing a screenshot image. The API will analyze the image and return detailed information about the anime, including the episode, timestamp, and title.
Input: Required. Base64 encoded image file. 
Output: The function will return a JSON object containing the following information: 
- Anilist ID: Integer. The ID of the anime on Anilist.
- Filename: String. The name of the file that was uploaded.
- Episode: Integer. The episode number where the scene appears.
- From: Float. The timestamp where the scene starts.
- To: Float. The timestamp where the scene ends.
- Token: String. A unique token that can be used to retrieve more information about the anime.

2. Name: Get Metadata
Description: This function allows users to retrieve detailed metadata for a particular episode of an anime. Users must provide the Anilist ID and episode number as input.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- Anilist ID: Integer. The ID of the anime on Anilist.
- Episode: Integer. The episode number to retrieve metadata for.
Output: The function will return a JSON object containing the following information:
- Title: String. The title of the anime.
- Title (native): String. The native title of the anime.
- Episode: Integer. The episode number.
- Season: Integer. The season number.
- Description: String. A brief description of the episode.
- Duration: Integer. The duration of the episode in seconds.
- Airdate: String. The airdate of the episode.
- Cover Image: String. The URL of the cover image for the episode.
- Characters: Array. An array of characters that appear in the episode.
- Staff: Array. An array of staff members who worked on the episode.

3. Name: Get Recommendations
Description: This function allows users to view related media recommendations based on the anime in question. Users must provide the Anilist ID as input.
Input: Required. Anilist ID: Integer. The ID of the anime on Anilist.
Output: The function will return a JSON object containing an array of recommended media. Each recommended media object will contain the following information:
- Title: String. The title of the recommended media.
- Type: String. The type of media (e.g. anime, manga, light novel).
- Cover Image: String. The URL of the cover image for the recommended media.
- Anilist ID: Integer. The ID of the recommended media on Anilist.

Name: Bittrex
Description: Next Generation Crypto Trading Platform
Introduction: The Bittrex API (Application Programming Interface) is a powerful tool for developers and traders who are looking to integrate cryptocurrency trading into their applications. Bittrex is a next-generation crypto trading platform that allows users to buy, sell, and trade cryptocurrencies with ease. With the Bittrex API, developers can access a range of functions, including: 1) Retrieving real-time market data, including order books, trades, and ticker information. 2) Placing orders and managing trades. 3) Accessing account information and balances. The API is designed for maximum flexibility and ease of use, making it a great choice for developers who want to build crypto trading applications.
Functions:
1. Name: Get Markets
Description: Retrieves a list of all available markets on Bittrex.
Input: None
Output: Returns an array of market objects, each containing the market symbol, base currency, quote currency, minimum trade size, and other market-specific information.

2. Name: Get Ticker
Description: Retrieves the latest ticker information for a specified market.
Input: Required. String. The market symbol in the format of "BASEQUOTE", where BASE is the base currency and QUOTE is the quote currency.
Output: Returns a ticker object containing the market symbol, last trade price, bid and ask prices, 24-hour high and low prices, and other market-specific information.

3. Name: Get Order Book
Description: Retrieves the current order book for a specified market.
Input: Required. String. The market symbol in the format of "BASEQUOTE", where BASE is the base currency and QUOTE is the quote currency. Optional. Integer. The depth of the order book to retrieve, up to a maximum of 500.
Output: Returns an order book object containing the current bid and ask orders, as well as their respective quantities and prices.

4. Name: Get Trade History
Description: Retrieves the trade history for a specified market.
Input: Required. String. The market symbol in the format of "BASEQUOTE", where BASE is the base currency and QUOTE is the quote currency. Optional. Integer. The number of trades to retrieve, up to a maximum of 200.
Output: Returns an array of trade objects, each containing the trade ID, timestamp, price, quantity, and other trade-specific information.

5. Name: Place Limit Order
Description: Places a limit order to buy or sell a specified market at a specified price and quantity.
Input: Required. String. The market symbol in the format of "BASEQUOTE", where BASE is the base currency and QUOTE is the quote currency. Required. String. The order type, either "buy" or "sell". Required. Number. The price at which to place the order. Required. Number. The quantity of the order to place.
Output: Returns an order object containing the order ID, timestamp, market symbol, order type, price, quantity, and other order-specific information.

6. Name: Cancel Order
Description: Cancels a previously placed order.
Input: Required. String. The order ID to cancel.
Output: Returns a boolean indicating whether the order was successfully cancelled.

7. Name: Get Order
Description: Retrieves information about a previously placed order.
Input: Required. String. The order ID to retrieve.
Output: Returns an order object containing the order ID, timestamp, market symbol, order type, price, quantity, and other order-specific information.

8. Name: Get Open Orders
Description: Retrieves a list of all open orders for a specified market or for all markets.
Input: Optional. String. The market symbol in the format of "BASEQUOTE", where BASE is the base currency and QUOTE is the quote currency. If not specified, returns all open orders for all markets.
Output: Returns an array of order objects, each containing the order ID, timestamp, market symbol, order type, price, quantity, and other order-specific information.

9. Name: Get Account Balances
Description: Retrieves the current balances for all currencies in the user's account.
Input: None
Output: Returns an array of balance objects, each containing the currency symbol, total balance, available balance, and other balance-specific information.

The API provides multiple functions for retrieving information about live events, including: 1) search for events by keyword, location, date, or genre. 2) access detailed information about specific events such as performers, date, time, and location. 3) retrieve information about venues, such as address, seating maps, and upcoming events. Name: iTunes Search

Introduction: The iTunes Search API is a powerful tool for software developers who want to integrate iTunes Store content into their applications. It provides a range of functions to query for products, including apps, music, movies, TV shows, audiobooks, and more. Some of the primary functions offered by this API include: 1) Search for products with specific keywords, categories, or artist names. 2) Retrieve product details, such as pricing, descriptions, and artwork. 3) Access to reviews, ratings, and user feedback. This API also allows developers to access affiliate links for products, which can provide additional revenue opportunities. It is a great resource for any application that wants to offer iTunes Store content to its users.

Description: This function allows users to search for products in the iTunes Store based on specific keywords, categories, or artist names.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- term: String. The search term to query for.
- country: String. The two-letter country code for the store you want to search in.
- media: String. The type of media you want to search for (e.g. movie, podcast, music).
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a product that matches the search query. Each object contains information such as the product's name, artist, price, and artwork.

2. Name: lookup

- id: Integer. The unique identifier for the product you want to retrieve details for.
- country: String. The two-letter country code for the store you want to search in.
- media: String. The type of media you want to retrieve details for (e.g. movie, podcast, music).
Output: A JSON object representing the product that matches the specified ID. The object contains information such as the product's name, artist, price, and artwork.

3. Name: reviews
Description: This function allows users to retrieve reviews and ratings for a specific product in the iTunes Store.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. The unique identifier for the product you want to retrieve reviews for.
- country: String. The two-letter country code for the store you want to search in.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a review for the specified product. Each object contains information such as the review's text, rating, and author.

4. Name: affiliateLink
Description: This function allows users to generate an affiliate link for a specific product in the iTunes Store, which can provide additional revenue opportunities.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. The unique identifier for the product you want to generate an affiliate link for.
- country: String. The two-letter country code for the store you want to search in.
Output: A string representing the affiliate link for the specified product.

Name: Freelancer
Description: Hire freelancers to get work done
Introduction: The Freelancer API is an online platform where businesses can connect with freelancers to get their work done. With a simple integration into your application, the API provides access to a wide range of features, including: 1) Search for freelancers with the required skills. 2) Post projects and receive proposals from freelancers. 3) Management of projects and payments. 4) Get real-time notifications on project updates. Whether it's a small task or a complex project, Freelancer API is an ideal choice for businesses looking for reliable and cost-effective solutions to meet their project requirements.
Functions:
1. Name: searchFreelancers
Description: This function allows businesses to search for freelancers based on their skills and other criteria.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- keywords: String. Keywords related to the project.
- skills: String. Skills required for the project.
- country: String. Country where the freelancer is located.
- hourly_rate_min: Integer. Minimum hourly rate of the freelancer.
- hourly_rate_max: Integer. Maximum hourly rate of the freelancer.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a freelancer. Each object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the freelancer.
- username: String. Username of the freelancer.
- display_name: String. Display name of the freelancer.
- profile_picture_url: String. URL of the freelancer's profile picture.
- hourly_rate: Integer. Hourly rate of the freelancer.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills of the freelancer.
- country: String. Country where the freelancer is located.

2. Name: postProject
Description: This function allows businesses to post a project and receive proposals from freelancers.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- title: String. Title of the project.
- description: String. Description of the project.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills required for the project.
- budget: Integer. Budget for the project.
- currency: String. Currency of the budget.
- duration: Integer. Duration of the project in days.
Output: JSON object representing the posted project. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the project.
- title: String. Title of the project.
- description: String. Description of the project.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills required for the project.
- budget: Integer. Budget for the project.
- currency: String. Currency of the budget.
- duration: Integer. Duration of the project in days.
- status: String. Status of the project.

3. Name: getProject
Description: This function allows businesses to retrieve information about a specific project.
Input: Required. Integer representing the project ID.
Output: JSON object representing the project. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the project.
- title: String. Title of the project.
- description: String. Description of the project.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills required for the project.
- budget: Integer. Budget for the project.
- currency: String. Currency of the budget.
- duration: Integer. Duration of the project in days.
- status: String. Status of the project.

4. Name: updateProject
Description: This function allows businesses to update information about a specific project.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the project.
- title: String. Title of the project.
- description: String. Description of the project.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills required for the project.
- budget: Integer. Budget for the project.
- currency: String. Currency of the budget.
- duration: Integer. Duration of the project in days.
Output: JSON object representing the updated project. The object contains the same keys as the getProject function.

5. Name: getProposals
Description: This function allows businesses to retrieve proposals for a specific project.
Input: Required. Integer representing the project ID.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a proposal. Each object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the proposal.
- bidder_id: Integer. Unique identifier of the freelancer who submitted the proposal.
- bidder_username: String. Username of the freelancer who submitted the proposal.
- bid_amount: Integer. Amount proposed by the freelancer.
- bid_duration: Integer. Duration proposed by the freelancer in days.
- bid_time: String. Time when the proposal was submitted.

6. Name: acceptProposal
Description: This function allows businesses to accept a proposal for a specific project.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the proposal.
- project_id: Integer. Unique identifier of the project.
Output: JSON object representing the accepted proposal. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the proposal.
- bidder_id: Integer. Unique identifier of the freelancer who submitted the proposal.
- bidder_username: String. Username of the freelancer who submitted the proposal.
- bid_amount: Integer. Amount proposed by the freelancer.
- bid_duration: Integer. Duration proposed by the freelancer in days.
- bid_time: String. Time when the proposal was submitted.
- status: String. Status of the proposal.

7. Name: getNotifications
Description: This function allows businesses to retrieve real-time notifications on project updates.

- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the notification.
- type: String. Type of the notification.
- message: String. Message of the notification.
- time: String. Time when the notification was sent.

  - field: String. The name of the field to sort on.
  - direction: String. The direction to sort in ("asc" or "desc").
- limit: Optional. Integer. The maximum number of results to return.
- offset: Optional. Integer. The number of results to skip before returning the first result.
